Research Overview

Research question

Which genes in rice shoots change their expression when seedlings are exposed to drought for three days, and in which direction (up or down) do they change?

Key findings
  • Differential expression. Of 43,474 probes tested, 21,346 (49.1%) passed both the statistical (BH-adjusted P < 0.05) and effect-size (|logFC| ≥ 1) criteria. 11,550 probes (54.1%) were upregulated and 9,796 (45.9%) were downregulated under drought.
  • Effect sizes. 9,953 significant probes had an absolute logFC of at least 2, and 5,153 had an absolute logFC of at least 3. These values are reported on the original analysis scale; they are not interpreted as specific fold changes because the logarithm base has not been confirmed.
  • Expression patterns. The MDS plot and heatmap can be used to assess whether samples show patterns associated with their experimental groups. Their interpretation is described in the relevant sections.
  • Functional annotations. Keyword counts for LEA proteins, dehydrins, heat shock proteins and other annotation categories are presented as descriptive observations, not as formal pathway-enrichment results.
  • Interpretation note. The analysis uses four control and four drought arrays. The sample size, common-reference design and expression scale should be considered when interpreting the results.

1. Introduction

Rice (Oryza sativa) is a staple food for more than half of the world’s population, and it is also one of the more water-demanding cereal crops. Drought is therefore an important environmental factor limiting rice yield. When a rice plant experiences water deficit, it can adjust the activity of many genes. Protective proteins may accumulate, growth-related and photosynthesis-related processes may change, and signalling and transcription-factor networks may be reprogrammed (Gupta et al., 2020; Todaka et al., 2015).

Microarrays measure the abundance of thousands of transcripts at the same time. Comparing stressed and unstressed plants can therefore help identify genes whose expression differs between the conditions. Public repositories such as the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) make these data available for re-analysis (Edgar et al., 2002).

This project re-analyses the public GEO dataset GSE115826 (“Rice drought treatment”), in which shoots of two-week-old Nipponbare seedlings were sampled after three days of drought or well-watered treatment. Differential expression was tested with the limma package in R (Ritchie et al., 2015), and the results were visualised and annotated using the GPL6864 platform description.

2. Research Objectives

The overall aim is to identify the molecular response of rice shoots to drought stress using differential gene expression analysis. The specific objectives are:

  1. To obtain the GSE115826 dataset from NCBI GEO and examine its quality, including missing values, infinite values, duplicate probes and zero-variance probes.
  2. To assign each sample to the Control or Drought group using its metadata.
  3. To explore the data with a sample-level summary, an expression boxplot and an MDS plot.
  4. To test every retained probe for differential expression between drought and control using limma with empirical Bayes moderation and Benjamini-Hochberg correction.
  5. To identify significant, upregulated and downregulated probes using adjusted P < 0.05 and |logFC| ≥ 1.
  6. To visualise the results with a volcano plot and a heatmap, and to annotate probes with GPL6864 platform information.
  7. To describe the main expression patterns in relation to known drought-response mechanisms, while recognising the limitations of annotation-based interpretation.

4. Methodology

4.1 Analytical workflow

Data acquisition
GSE115826 series matrix loaded with GEOquery.
Group assignment
Control and Drought labels assigned from sample metadata.
Quality control
Missing, infinite, duplicate and zero-variance checks.
Expression preprocessing
Invalid and zero-variance probes removed while retaining original expression values.
Exploration
Sample summary, boxplot and MDS plot.
Linear model
limma lmFit, Drought − Control contrast and eBayes.
Thresholding
BH adjusted P < 0.05 and |logFC| ≥ 1.
Visualisation and annotation
Volcano plot, heatmap and GPL6864 annotation.

4.2 Data loading and group assignment

The series matrix was loaded with the GEOquery package (Davis & Meltzer, 2007) into an ExpressionSet, from which the expression matrix and sample metadata were extracted. Samples were assigned to Control or Drought using the study metadata. The resulting group counts were 4 control and 4 drought arrays.

4.3 Preprocessing and expression values

The expression values were obtained from the NCBI GEO Series Matrix file. The dataset contains Agilent Feature Extraction LogRatio measurements.

The original GEO values were retained during preprocessing. Probes containing non-finite values and probes with zero variance across the samples were removed before differential expression analysis.

No additional logarithmic scale conversion was applied. The exact logarithm base of the deposited LogRatio values should not be assumed without confirmation from the original platform documentation.

The resulting expression matrix was used as the input for the limma analysis.

4.4 Differential expression with limma

A linear model with one mean per group (no intercept) was fitted to every probe. The Drought − Control contrast was extracted, and the standard errors were moderated with empirical Bayes (Smyth, 2004; Ritchie et al., 2015).

design <- model.matrix(~ 0 + condition)
contrast <- makeContrasts(Drought - Control, levels = design)
fit <- lmFit(clean_expression, design)
fit2 <- eBayes(contrasts.fit(fit, contrast))
results <- topTable(
  fit2,
  coef = 1,
  number = Inf,
  adjust.method = "BH",
  sort.by = "P"
)

A positive logFC means that the measured expression value is higher under drought relative to control. A negative logFC means that it is lower under drought. The interpretation of the numerical magnitude depends on the scale of the input expression values. P-values were adjusted for multiple testing across all probes with the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure (Benjamini & Hochberg, 1995).

4.5 Significance criteria

Category Rule
Significant adj. P < 0.05 and |logFC| ≥ 1
Upregulated Significant and logFC ≥ 1
Downregulated Significant and logFC ≤ −1
Not significant All other probes

4.6 Visualisation and annotation

The volcano plot (ggplot2; Wickham, 2016) displays logFC against −log10 adjusted P for every probe. The heatmap (pheatmap; Kolde) displays the most variable probes, with each row scaled to its own mean and standard deviation if row scaling was applied in the analysis script. Significant probes were joined to the GPL6864 annotation table by probe ID to obtain locus identifiers and functional descriptions.

5.3 Multidimensional scaling (MDS)

The MDS plot places samples according to expression differences between them. Samples with more similar expression profiles are positioned closer together.

The MDS plot can be used to examine whether samples separate according to their experimental conditions and whether any sample appears distinct from the others. The observed pattern should be interpreted directly from the plotted sample positions.

6. Differential Expression Analysis

Model summary
Probes tested43,474
Samples in the model8 (4 vs 4)
ContrastDrought − Control
ModerationEmpirical Bayes (eBayes)
Multiple-testing correctionBenjamini-Hochberg (FDR)
Probes with adj. P < 0.0532,661 (75.1%)
Smallest adjusted P-value2.14e-09
Probes passing both thresholds21,346 (49.1%)

Of the 43,474 probes tested, 32,661 had an adjusted P-value below 0.05. Requiring in addition an absolute logFC of at least 1 reduced this to 21,346 probes. The effect-size threshold was applied to identify probes with larger differences on the original analysis scale.

8. Visualizations

8.1 Volcano plot

Each point represents one probe. Positive logFC values indicate higher measured expression under drought, while negative values indicate lower measured expression under drought. The horizontal and vertical thresholds identify probes that satisfy the selected statistical and effect-size criteria.

8.2 Expression heatmap

The heatmap provides a visual comparison of expression patterns across the samples. Similarity between samples and groups can be examined from the clustering pattern. The heatmap should be interpreted together with the sample metadata and MDS plot.

9. Discussion

Differential expression under drought. The analysis identifies 21,346 probes that meet the selected adjusted P-value and absolute logFC thresholds. The relative numbers of upregulated and downregulated probes provide an overview of the direction of the measured expression differences. The MDS plot and heatmap provide additional visual evidence for assessing similarities and differences among the samples.

Protective proteins and stress response. The annotation keyword analysis identifies probes whose descriptions contain terms associated with LEA proteins, dehydrins and heat shock proteins. These protein families have recognised roles in plant stress responses, including protection against cellular dehydration and protein damage (Todaka et al., 2015). However, keyword matching alone does not establish that a complete biological pathway is significantly activated.

Growth and photosynthesis-related annotations. The annotation table also includes terms related to chloroplasts, photosystems, expansins and aquaporins. These categories may provide useful starting points for investigating how drought affects photosynthesis, growth and water transport. The direction of the measured logFC values should be examined for each annotated probe before drawing conclusions.

Other strongly changing probes. The strongest upregulated and downregulated probes are presented in Sections 7.3 and 7.4. Their annotations can help identify candidates for further investigation. Probe annotations should be checked against current rice gene databases before assigning specific biological functions.

Interpretation of effect sizes. The original GEO LogRatio values were retained, and their exact logarithm base has not been confirmed here. Therefore, logFC values are reported without interpreting them as specific two-fold, four-fold or eight-fold changes. The selected thresholds are used as numerical effect-size criteria on the original analysis scale.

10. Limitations

  • Small sample size. Only four biological replicates per group were available. The experiment covers one cultivar (Nipponbare), one tissue (shoot) and one time point (day 3). The results cannot show how the response changes over time or in other genotypes.
  • Common-reference design. The study uses a two-colour microarray design. The reference and sample labelling details should be interpreted using the original GEO metadata and raw data documentation.
  • Variability between groups. Differences in expression spread between the control and drought arrays may affect the statistical model and should be considered when interpreting P-values.
  • Preprocessing and normalisation. This analysis uses the expression values deposited in the GEO series matrix. The preprocessing and normalisation performed by the original study should be considered when interpreting the results.
  • Probe-level results. Results are reported per probe, not necessarily per unique gene. Several probes may represent the same locus.
  • Annotation limitations. Some probes may have hypothetical or unknown-function annotations. The keyword-based functional summary is descriptive and is not a formal Gene Ontology or pathway enrichment analysis.
  • Expression scale. The exact logarithm base of the deposited LogRatio values has not been confirmed. Therefore, the results are not interpreted as log2 fold changes.
  • No experimental validation. The findings have not been confirmed with an independent method such as qRT-PCR.

11. Conclusion

This study re-analysed the GEO dataset GSE115826 to investigate the response of rice shoots to three days of drought. After preprocessing, 43,474 probes were tested using the limma package. A total of 21,346 probes met the selected significance criteria (adjusted P < 0.05 and |logFC| ≥ 1), including 11,550 upregulated probes and 9,796 downregulated probes under drought.

The analysis provides a probe-level overview of expression differences between the control and drought conditions. The MDS plot, heatmap and annotation summaries provide additional information for exploring these differences.

Future work. Further analysis could include (i) formal Gene Ontology and pathway enrichment analysis, (ii) mapping probes to unique gene loci, (iii) comparison with other rice drought datasets, (iv) a sensitivity analysis using alternative preprocessing approaches, and (v) qRT-PCR validation of selected candidate genes.

C. How to reproduce the analysis

  1. Open Rice_Drought_ICA3.Rproj in RStudio.
  2. Run code/analysis.R from top to bottom. It should generate the CSV files in results/ and the figures in figures/.
  3. Open reports/final_report.Rmd and click Knit to generate the HTML report.
  4. Check that the generated tables, numerical results and figures correspond to the latest analysis outputs.
